title: squarespace.list_orders
description: Input/output contract for listing orders. GET /orders on the commerce base URL (https://api.squarespace.com/1.0/commerce). VERIFICATION STATUS: the response envelope is verified against fixtures/orders.json — note the top-level array key is `result`, NOT `orders`, unlike list_products (`products`) and get_contact's list form (`contacts`). The per-order fields are now CONFIRMED live, 2026-08-16, against a real populated order — the store had zero orders when the envelope was first verified, but list_orders has since been re-run against the real order created via create_order that same day. The populated response exactly matches create_order's captured response shape (same fields, same nesting, same line-item shape) — see fixtures/orders.json and fixtures/create-order-response.json. One confirmed difference from create_order's output: list_orders' per-order objects do NOT include an `idempotencyKey` field — that field is specific to the create_order response.

input.title: ListOrdersInput
input.description: All fields optional. CONFIRMED live, 2026-08-16, against all four cursor combinations directly (a 56-order store was built to produce a real pagination cursor to test against): cursor + limit succeeds; cursor + modifiedAfter/modifiedBefore and cursor + fulfillmentStatus are both rejected with 400 INVALID_REQUEST_ERROR.INVALID_ARGUMENT, "Cursor cannot be set while other parameters are present." So `cursor` specifically excludes `modifiedAfter`, `modifiedBefore`, and `fulfillmentStatus` — but NOT `limit`. This is narrower than list_products' confirmed rule that cursor must be the only parameter sent; don't assume the two endpoints share the same restriction. Separately, `modifiedAfter` and `modifiedBefore` are CONFIRMED live to require pairing — sending one without the other is rejected with 400 INVALID_REQUEST_ERROR.MISSING_ARGUMENT, "'modifiedBefore' and 'modifiedAfter' must both be specified." (This pairing requirement was previously removed from validation as unconfirmed; live evidence has now reinstated it.)

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's pagination.nextPageCursor.

modifiedAfter.description: ISO 8601. May be used alone or alongside modifiedBefore.

modifiedBefore.description: ISO 8601. May be used alone or alongside modifiedAfter.

cursor.description: CONFIRMED live, 2026-08-16 — cursor excludes modifiedAfter, modifiedBefore, and fulfillmentStatus specifically (400 INVALID_REQUEST_ERROR.INVALID_ARGUMENT, "Cursor cannot be set while other parameters are present."). limit is NOT excluded — cursor + limit is confirmed to succeed.

result.description: Verified key name — the orders endpoint uses `result`, not `orders`.

examples.description: CONFIRMED live, 2026-08-16 — the real captured response from an unfiltered GET /orders call, matching fixtures/orders-populated.json byte for byte except customerEmail, which is replaced with a placeholder. This is the same order captured in create-order.schema.json's example, confirmed to match exactly (see connector.yaml's known_limitations).

Illustrates the input shape with all three optional filters combined (a valid combination — none of these three are mutually exclusive with each other). The empty `result`/pagination output itself is real, matching fixtures/orders.json, captured when the store had zero orders — at that point any valid query trivially returned empty, so this exact filter combination was not itself separately exercised against a real match/no-match case.
